final_answer: >>> Ice floats on water due to its unique molecular structure, which is governed by hydrogen bonding. When water freezes, its molecules arrange into a hexagonal crystalline lattice, held together by hydrogen bonds. These bonds form a rigid, open framework that creates more space between the molecules compared to the more densely packed structure of liquid water. As a result, ice is less dense than liquid water, allowing it to float. This phenomenon is unusual because most substances become denser when solidified, but water’s hydrogen bonding leads to this exception.
